findings.description: Removing the already_bracketed guard means an optional option whose metavar is already bracketed (e.g. metavar="[FOO]") is now wrapped again, rendering "[[FOO]]" in the usage line.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an optional option declared with metavar="[FOO]" (not required). Before, already_bracketed was true so the metavar was left as "[FOO]". After this change, the condition is only not self.required, so var becomes "[[FOO]]". Impact: the usage/help output shows doubled brackets for such options, a visible regression for users who relied on the previous behavior.
